text:
anna: FYI support ticket from ACME — p95 jumped ~3.5x after runtime v3.2 rollout. customer impact: API generation latency spikes for their larger-prompt cohort (cohort=B ~3% traffic). rollout at 03:45Z yesterday, first alerts ~04:20Z. anyone else seeing cohort-specific tail?
raj: on it. can you paste the raw p95/p99 series and which regions/pods are affected?
anna: quick prometheus snippet (5m window):
```
sum by (cohort) (histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, cohort)))
```
cohort=B shows 0.42s; baseline ~0.12s. p99 moved from 0.22s -> 0.85s.
maria: canary dashboards didn't flag this during canary. looks prod-only. any config diffs between canary and prod?
jeff: deploy-bot shows runtime/v3.2 applied with a kernel-selector tweak + adaptive batching enabled in prod only. deploy-bot: "apply(runtime/v3.2) -> prod @ 2025-10-11T03:45Z"
raj: adaptive batching + kernel selector changes are suspect. that can increase tail for certain seq distributions. did prod change max_batch_size or grouping?
anna: prod config: MAX_BATCH=64, canary=32. PR note: "enable adaptive_grouping=true" targeted prod.
maria: repro plan: replay cohort B synthetic workload against v3.1 and v3.2 flags toggled. who can run replay?
jeff: kicking replay on staging with identical model and flags. ETA ~12m.
oncall: if customer impact is high we should traffic-split or rollback. support says intermittent but persistent p95 >300ms for ~2h.
support-bot: customer ticket #8765 linked: https://support/acme/8765 (summary attached)
raj: bisect approach: flip adaptive_grouping=false for a tiny prod cohort (0.5%) and measure p95 delta. if improved, flip globally.
anna: noted. also check KV cache hit rates — larger batches may change cache eviction and warmup patterns. logs show increased kv_cache miss for cohort B after rollout.
maria: logs snippet:
```
[2025-10-11T04:22:17Z] pod runtime-abc kernel-selector v3.2: kv_cache.miss=0.37 rate=72/s
[2025-10-11T04:22:18Z] pod runtime-def kv_cache.miss=0.12 rate=68/s
```
jeff: kernel-selector seems to pick a different kernel path for longer contexts which may evict caches faster. makes sense with bigger batching.
raj: mitigation options: 1) rollback kernel-selector tweak 2) reduce MAX_BATCH to canary value 3) traffic-split cohort B to v3.1-old 4) hotfix to KV cache sizing/tuning.
oncall: prefer non-rollback immediate: traffic-split a small portion to old variant for cohort B + monitor 30m; rollback if not improved.
anna: applying traffic split now: route 95% cohort B -> v3.2, 5% -> v3.1-old for measurement.
deploy-bot: Traffic-split applied: cohort=B 5%->v3.1-old @ 2025-10-11T04:40Z
maria: early numbers after split: p95 down 420ms -> 180ms in cohort B within 6m. KV cache hit ratio improved on the 5% v3.1-old path.
raj: that's strong signal. root cause likely interaction between adaptive_grouping (batching) and kernel-selector path causing cache thrash for certain sequence-length cohorts.
jeff: I'll open a change PR to revert adaptive_grouping in prod and align MAX_BATCH across envs, plus add a targeted canary job that replays cohort-length distributions.
anna: thanks. I'll update customer and mark ticket as "investigating - mitigated by traffic split". :thumbsup:
maria: capture this in a short postmortem and add automated alert for sudden cohort-specific p95 diffs (cohort delta > 2x baseline).
oncall: tagging for follow-up in eng-runtime weekly sync.
anna: follow-ups: (1) PR to change config, (2) canary replay job, (3) kernel-path histograms, (4) postmortem draft. I'll own customer comms.
raj: also add a small experiment to measure KV cache pressure when batch_size increases (run microbench with seq-length distribution).
jeff: opened PR #4521 (revert adaptive_grouping in prod) and job ticket RT-789 to add cohort replay.
anna: great work team — will circle back when postmortem + customer update done.
